extracted.intended_audience: researchers and developer teams registering or developing reporting guidelines (guideline developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers or groups who are developing reporting guidelines (checklists, flow diagrams, or structured texts) and want to register their project with the EQUATOR Network. Covers what may/may not be registered, reasons to register, responsibilities, and the registration process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a reporting guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: "A reporting guideline is a checklist, flow diagram, or structured text to guide authors in reporting a specific type of research, developed using explicit methodology."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used to determine whether a project is appropriate for registration on the EQUATOR register of reporting guidelines under development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible item: development of a reporting guideline for a research article
rubrics_metrics.description: You can register the development of a reporting guideline for a research article published in a scientific journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project should be about reporting guidance for articles (not clinical practice guidance), and it should be under development (not finished).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible materials to register
rubrics_metrics.description: You can register: the development of a checklist or statement, the explanation and elaboration (E&E) document under development, the protocol of your project, the website dedicated to this development and other associated materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any associated materials that are part of the reporting guideline development so the register entry represents the broader project outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: reporting project progress updates
rubrics_metrics.description: You can register the progress of your work, by sending us news about steps finished, such as the publication of protocols or systematic reviews, the start of Delphi surveys and consensus meetings scheduled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the register to keep the entry up to date with milestones to show ongoing development and attract collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited: clinical guidelines for clinical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot register clinical guidelines: guidance you are developing for clinical practice in any field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical practice guidelines are out of scope for this register; do not submit them here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited: guidance for the conduct of research or methodological guidelines (unless part of a reporting guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot register guidance for the conduct of research or methodological guidelines, unless they are part of a reporting guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the methodological guidance forms an integral component of a reporting guideline for research articles it may be eligible; standalone methodological or conduct guidance is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited: translation of existing reporting guidelines (pre-completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot register the translation of existing reporting guidelines (but you can request for the translation, once complete, to be added to the relevant reporting guideline record in our main database).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations should be submitted to the main database once finished; initial translation projects are not accepted on this 'under development' register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited: guidance/checklists developed specifically for critical appraisal or evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot register guidance or checklists developed specifically for the critical appraisal or evaluation of the reporting of health research studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools intended for appraisal/evaluation (rather than guiding authors' reporting) are out of scope for this register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited: guidance whose development has already finished
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot register guidance whose development has already finished, even if not yet published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The register is for projects under active development; completed guidance should be submitted to the main EQUATOR database when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited: guidance on internal communication or reports not intended for scientific publication
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot register guidance on the quality of communication between healthcare providers, such as pathology or laboratory reports or medical records, or any report not intended for publication as a scientific paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only guidance intended to improve reporting of research for publication is eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: seek permission from original development group for extensions/translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The EQUATOR Network recommends that authors seek permission from the original development group if they plan to develop an extension or translation of an existing reporting guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any extensions or translation requests will be sent to the original development group for their approval before posting on the EQUATOR website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to register (awareness, prevent duplication, transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why register? To raise awareness, to prevent duplication of effort, and to be transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registering can attract collaborators, helps others avoid duplicating the same work (and may enable joining existing groups), and allows publication/dissemination of protocols or simple statements so development methods are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and disclaimer regarding endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration does not imply endorsement by the EQUATOR Network; the contents of the reporting guidelines under development listed here are their authors’ responsibility, and no liability is accepted for any use of reporting guidelines under development information included in these pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure they have appropriate authority to develop the reporting guideline and that submitted information is accurate to the best of their knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration process and form completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Please register your planned guideline using the provided Registration document (word). Please take care to fill in all fields, as incomplete forms may be returned to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete information so EQUATOR can summarise it for publication and verify the project is about developing a reporting guideline (not methodological/clinical guidance) and assess duplication/overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: EQUATOR editorial discretion and non-exhaustive coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: This list is not an exhaustive collection of reporting guidelines under development, and the EQUATOR Network may include or remove any reporting guideline under development from these pages at any time at its sole discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume inclusion; provide links or notify EQUATOR of known projects if missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for developing reporting guidelines (toolkit resource)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for developing reporting guidelines: Visit the EQUATOR Network toolkit on how to develop a reporting guideline for essential information and advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The toolkit provides essential information and advice on methodology and best practice for developing reporting guidelines; developers are directed to consult it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification: common reporting guideline topics and main guideline families
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting guidelines for main study types are listed (e.g., CONSORT for randomised trials, SPIRIT for study protocols, STROBE for observational studies, PRISMA for systematic reviews, STARD/TRIPOD for diagnostic/prognostic studies, CARE for case reports, ARRIVE for animal pre-clinical studies, SQUIRE for quality improvement, CHEERS for economic evaluations, SRQR/COREQ for qualitative research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EQUATOR organises and references common guideline families to help developers situate their work and check for existing or overlapping guidelines.
